result.title: External Observers May See More Clearly: Cross-Model Span-Level Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models via Hidden State Probing
result.summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly serve as foundational reasoning engines, their tendency to hallucinate remains a critical vulnerability. While recent internal state probes offer a promising alternative to slow external retrieval systems, they largely reduce hallucination detection to a token-wise binary classification task, failing to capture the structured, sequential boundaries of semantic drift. Here, we introduce an internal hidden state framework for fine-grained, span-level hallucination detection. By inspecting layer-wise activation patterns, we attempt to detect the exact hallucination onset and continuation tokens in an LLM generation. Our experiments show that this approach successfully isolates hallucination onsets, achieving substantial improvements in Precision-Recall AUC over random baselines despite extreme class imbalance. Ultimately, we propose a novel cross-model detection framework in which one model observes the internal representations elicited by another model's generation. We find that an external observer can match or exceed a generator's self-detection of its own hallucination onsets, including when the observer is the smaller model, suggesting that self-detection is not the ceiling for onset localisation.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出基于 LLM 隐藏状态的分层激活探针，将幻觉检测从 token 级二分类改为 span 级的幻觉起始与延续定位，并进一步提出跨模型探测框架，由外部模型观察另一模型生成时的内部表示。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽是纯文本方法，但其「从内部状态定位语义漂移起止点」和跨模型观察 hidden state 的思路，可能与 LVR 中推理状态的使用、停止与证据充分性判断及外部验证有关，可供核查迁移。
